title: Quantum Fisher information of magnetic quantum phase transition on Kondo lattice
authors: Yuan Fang, Lei Chen, Mounica Mahankali, Fang Xie, Yiming Wang, Shouvik Sur, Qimiao Si
abstract: Strange metals exemplify highly collective quantum many-body systems that call for new means of characterization, and there is considerable potential for quantum information approaches contributing to the cause. We investigate multipartite entanglement across the quantum phase transition of a Kondo lattice model using the quantum Fisher information (QFI). We show that the QFI associated with the spin components transverse to the order parameter characterizes the destruction of heavy quasiparticles in the Kondo-destroyed magnetic-ordered phase. The physical origin of this observation is elucidated through an analysis of the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model. We propose to test the results in terms of both unpolarized and polarized inelastic neutron scattering measurements in the ordered part of the heavy fermion phase diagram. Our findings illustrate how different operators of a many-body system can be employed to not only witness multipartite entanglement in different sectors and but also elucidate the overall physics across different parts of the phase diagram.
summary: The authors use Quantum Fisher Information to characterize multipartite entanglement across the quantum phase transition in the Kondo lattice model. They demonstrate that transverse spin correlations are necessary to witness this entanglement specifically in the magnetically ordered state. This provides a powerful tool for understanding complex many-body physics in heavy fermion materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how multipartite entanglement, quantified by the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), characterizes quantum phase transitions in strongly interacting magnetic systems.
main_result: The QFI associated with transverse spin components reveals multipartite entanglement in the magnetically ordered Kondo-destroyed phase, while longitudinal components remain trivial.
method: The analysis employs theoretical techniques including Extended Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (EDMFT), Spin Wave Theory, and calculating the QFI via analytic continuation of dynamic susceptibilities.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Kondo lattice Hamiltonian, which captures the competition between local moment coupling (Kondo effect) and RKKY interactions. Theoretical insights are also drawn from the quasi-2D Heisenberg $J_1$-$J_2$ model.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information density ($f_Q$), normalized QFI ($	ext{nQFI}$), transverse vs. longitudinal spin components ($\mathbf{c}_{S\pm x}, \mathbf{c}_{Sz}$), and the dynamical susceptibility $\chi''$.
important_parameters: The control parameter is $\delta = I/T_{0K}$, which tunes the system across different magnetic regimes, including the Kondo-destroyed AF phase ($\delta > \delta_m$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include using linear spin wave theory for the ordered phase and employing analytic continuation methods (Padé, maximum entropy) to extract real-frequency data from imaginary time simulations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate QFI behavior across the transition ($\delta$ dependence), temperature evolution of $	ext{nQFI}$ for different spin components in the AF phase, and comparisons between different numerical calculation methods (Padé vs. Maximum Entropy).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Kondo lattice model by first establishing the theoretical framework linking QFI to magnetic susceptibilities. It then applies this formalism across various regimes—paramagnetic, Fermi-liquid, and AF-ordered—to pinpoint which spin operators best witness entanglement in each phase.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete link between quantum information measures (QFI) and the fundamental physics of strongly correlated electron systems undergoing magnetic transitions, offering new diagnostic tools beyond standard thermodynamic measurements.
